title: Tidepool Turn
hook: Build a living tidepool on a five-by-five board, then watch the next tide move everything: the clever placement is the one that still works after the water returns.
audience: Players seeking calm, compact turn-based strategy with visible chain reactions and short replayable sessions.
core_loop: Choose one of two creature or rock tiles, place it with a forecast of the next tide, resolve one water movement, preserve compatible neighbours, and complete a six-tide run with a local score.

score_notes.demand: A paid minimalist placement-strategy comparable is visible, but the proposed ecological audience and purchase intent remain untested.
score_notes.distinctiveness: A shared forecasted movement step changes the placement problem; this difference has not been checked against all close competitors.
score_notes.fun_potential: Planning for the tide may create satisfying reversals, or simply obscure consequences; a prototype must decide.
score_notes.scope_fit: A fixed board bounds art and interaction, while cascade ordering, fairness and replay balance create meaningful implementation risk.
score_notes.distribution: The before-and-after tide transformation is a possible short visual hook; its readability and appeal are unmeasured.

evidence.claim: The inspected Steam listing presents ISLANDERS as a released paid minimalist strategy game with visible user review activity. It is a category comparable, not evidence of Tidepool Turn's sales potential.
The publisher's description links placement rewards to nearby buildings and describes repeated runs. Our moving-water step is a proposed mechanical difference, not a feature claimed by this source.

risks: The two evidence records describe one source and are not independent confirmation of demand.
Resolving several ecological effects can make outcomes feel arbitrary unless forecast and ordering are clear.
Procedural variety may be unbalanced or repetitive; a small tile set does not guarantee replay value.
The game should present fictional rules rather than imply scientific accuracy it has not established.
Working title and nearby tile-placement competitors require clearance and comparison.
next_test: If authorized, make a paper or greybox five-by-five board with three species and one deterministic tide rule. Observe five target players completing two six-tide runs. Continue if four can explain why one tile moved and three choose a different placement because of the forecast; hold or redesign if choices remain guesswork. Voluntary replay is recorded separately and fun remains unvalidated until observed.
decision_reason: Held after ecology/tile comparisons and unclear tide-decision value. Terrarium interest does not by itself validate this mechanic; preserve as an evergreen alternative.
commercial_hypothesis: Test a finite premium strategy toy with local seeded runs and no live-service promise. USD 3.99-5.99 is a preliminary price question, not a revenue forecast.

prototype_envelope.scope: One board, three species, rocks, one tide rule, deterministic forecast and two test seeds; no persistent ecosystem or content progression.

budget_note: Prototype estimate is unvalidated and excludes recruitment, commercial balance/content, final art/audio, compatibility QA, store work and release lead time. No spend authorized.
